ops.title: resolveClaudePhysicalPolicy pins FleetGeneration to the compile-time hard cut, so a topology change can never converge
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-30 by the adversarial pass over the cc-pool wedge fix, and confirmed against fusekit v1.20.0's source. This is the residual behind that fix, filed because closing it needs its own change.

## The pin

`internal/tenantfs/driver_factories.go:75`, inside `resolveClaudePhysicalPolicy`:

    if identity.Owner != SourceAuthorityFleetOwner ||
        identity.FleetGeneration != SourceAuthorityFleetGeneration ||
        identity.AuthorityGeneration != identity.FleetGeneration ||
        ...

`SourceAuthorityFleetGeneration` is a compile-time constant (`= 1`), while the holder builds identities with `FleetGeneration: declaration.FleetGeneration` taken from the STORED fleet (fusekit `holder/source_driver_child.go:118-124`). So the check only ever passes at generation 1.

## Two consequences

**1. A diverged stored declaration fails before the publish path runs.** Startup order, traced through the pinned source: `cmd/cc-pool-runtime-archive/main.go` `startHolder` runs `embeddedHolder.Start` (which blocks on `runtime.WaitReady`) and only reaches `tenantfs.PublishClaudeSourceFleet` at `main.go:87` afterwards. Inside that start, fusekit `holder/runtime.go:186` → `r.start` → `r.activate` loads the stored topology at `runtime.go:446` and resolves it at `:450` via `DriverFactories.sourceFleet` (`holder/source_driver_child.go:98`), which calls cc-pool's factory per declaration. A release that changes the compiled declaration therefore crash-loops on the OLD stored one before any gate can republish it.

**2. Advancing the generation makes it permanent.** An earlier revision of the wedge fix derived the publication from the stored generation (`Generation: stored + 1`, `ExpectedGeneration: stored`). That satisfies fusekit's catalog rules, but the moment it advances a fleet to generation 2 the driver factory refuses every subsequent start **even when the declarations match exactly** — a strictly worse wedge than the crash loop it was fixing, and the lane's own tests asserted that end state.

**Reverted for this reason** in `cfb50ab`: the publication is back at the hard-cut generation, and the shipped fix is the read-then-compare gate plus one re-read behind a race winner. Both halves carry mutation brackets (removing either re-wedges with the incident's own `catalog: tenant generation mismatch`). So today's live wedge is closed and no new one is opened, but a genuine topology change still cannot converge.

## What a real fix has to settle

- Whether `FleetGeneration` belongs in the driver identity check at all. It is catalog bookkeeping; the identity that matters is owner, authority, driver ID, driver config, and declaration digest. Dropping just that one clause is probably right, but `AuthorityGeneration != FleetGeneration` is checked against it and needs the same thought.
- How a genuinely old stored declaration is retired across a release boundary — the factory has to accept the compiled declaration while still refusing a foreign one, and the gate has to be able to advance the fleet once the factory tolerates it. The two changes only work together.</body>

ops.text: A release that changes the compiled Claude declaration starts cleanly against a catalog holding the previous declaration, with no manual state deletion

resolveClaudePhysicalPolicy accepts the compiled declaration at whatever fleet generation carries it, and still refuses an identity that differs in owner, authority, driver ID, driver config, or declaration digest
PublishClaudeSourceFleet can advance a diverged stored fleet without leaving a daemon the driver factory then refuses to start
A test drives the whole release-boundary path: publish declaration A, acknowledge, then start against compiled declaration B
